title: 🏛️ Ann Arbor Council: Events, Housing, Zoning & Glue Trap Ban - NewsBreak
text:
21 hours ago 📅 Ann Arbor Council: Events, Housing, Zoning & Glue Trap Ban
The Ann Arbor City Council will meet on Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:00 PM in the City Council Chambers on the second floor of Larcom City Hall, 301 E. Huron St.
You can watch live on CTN Channel 16 , AT&T Channel 99 , or online at a2gov.org/watchCTN . A replay is planned for Friday, October 9, 2026 at 8:00 PM (time may change).
How to speak at the meeting Public comment sign‑up is by phone on the day of the meeting:
Call the City Clerk’s Office: 734-794-6140 between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM You can speak in person or via Zoom Zoom options:
Phone: 877-853-5247 or 888-788-0099 , Meeting ID 942 1273 2148 Online link: a2gov.org/CouncilZoom Comment rules:
Normally 3 minutes per speaker , 45 minutes total If more than 30 speakers sign up: 2 minutes each You cannot give your time to someone else Zoom callers: press ★9 to raise your hand and ★6 to unmute when called The City can provide accommodations for people who need assistance speaking to Council Early agenda items Update from the Independent Community Police Oversight Commission (ICPOC) , presented by City Administrator Milton Dohoney Jr. Usual reports from Council, the Mayor, and the City Administrator Approval of September 22, 2026 regular meeting minutes Community events and street closures Council will vote on three event street closures:
Main Street Area Trick or Treat Parade Sunday, October 25, 2026, 9:00 AM–4:00 PM (CA-1, 26-1629 ) Thanksgiving Day Turkey Trot Thursday, November 26, 2026 (CA-2, 26-1628 ) KindleFest 2026 on Detroit Street between Catherine and Fifth Friday, December 4, 2026, 7:00 AM–11:30 PM (CA-3, 26-1630 ) Development and housing items University Inn Ann Arbor agreement , 2424 E Stadium Blvd (CA-4, 26-1505 ) – a development agreement supported by a July 21, 2026 staff report and Planning Commission minutes. Affordable housing items:
Purchase of 6 Park View Place for affordable housing by the Ann Arbor Housing Development Corporation (CA-12, 26-1379 ) $500,000.00 grant to the same corporation to support a sustainable and affordable housing project at 2810 Boardwalk (CA-14, 26-1622 , 8 votes required ) Professional services, bridges, markets, and parks Council will consider several contracts:
Stantec Consulting Michigan Inc. : Professional services, $786,499.00 (CA-5, 26-1637 , 8 votes required ) Market Ventures, Inc. : Visioning and engagement plan for the Ann Arbor Farmers Market Contract $416,829.00 , plus accepting and appropriating $248,000.00 (CA-6, 26-1614 , 8 votes required ) OHM Advisors, Inc. : Engineering services for the South Barton Bridge Project , $407,824.00 (CA-8, 26-1616 ) Park naming:
Proposal to rename 2570 Dexter Avenue Park to Dr. George Henry Jewett II Park (CA-7, 26-1615 ), sponsored by the Park Advisory Commission . Airport lease At the Ann Arbor Municipal Airport , Council will consider (CA-9, 26-1536 ):
A 20‑year lease with Experimental Aircraft Association (EAA) Chapter 333 for Hangar Building 25 , and Old Terminal Building 26 Supporting documents include cost estimates and a draft lease Delinquent bills and special assessments Two resolutions deal with unpaid charges being added to tax bills:
Delinquent municipal utility charges (CA-10, 26-1548 ), with a water schedule attached Delinquent solid waste, board‑up, clean‑up, vacant property inspection, housing inspection, false alarm, and fire inspection fees as special assessments (CA-11, 26-1549 ), with detailed schedules Sustainability and energy items Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum grant (CA-13, 26-1404 ): $450,000.00 to improve and decarbonize the Energy House at Leslie Science & Nature Center , plus support for sustainability education and engagement ( 8 votes required ) DTE Electric easement (CA-15, 26-1430 ): Granting DTE an easement for electrical facilities at 3225 Sunnywood Drive , related to the Lakewood Nature Area ( 8 votes required ) Public hearings and major ordinances Two public hearings will accept comments (same Zoom call‑in rules as public comment):
PH-1 / B-1 – South State Street Rezoning
2080 South State Street Rezoning 1.199 acres from TWP (Township District) to O (Office District) ORD-26-23 , with staff reports, Planning Commission minutes, and maps Planning Commission recommended approval, 9–0 PH-2 / B-2 – Sustainable Energy Utility Rates
ORD-26-26 would amend Section 2:413 (Rate Schedules) in Chapter 35 (Sustainable Energy Utility) of the City Code New zoning and glue trap ban – first readings C-1 – The Dean II Rezoning, 548 S Fifth Ave
Rezoning 0.17 acres from R4C (Multiple-Family Dwelling) to D1 (Downtown Core), Midtown Character, Secondary Street Planning Commission recommended approval, 7–0 (ORD 26-1519 ) C-2 – Glue Trap Ban
Would add Chapter 98 (Glue Trap Ban) to Title VII (Businesses and Trades) of the City Code Sponsored by Councilmembers Ghazi Edwin, Briggs, and Cornell (ORD 26-1556 ) Other business, closed session, and filed minutes Time is set aside for New Business from Council (DC), Boards and Commissions (DB), and Staff (DS). Specific items are not listed in this packet. Council may go into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act for: Labor negotiations strategy Purchase or lease of real property Pending litigation Attorney/client privileged communications Citing MCL 15.268 (8)(1)(C), (D), (E), and (H) Minutes filed for the record:
Commission on Disability Issues – June 17, 2026 (F-1, 26-1090 ) Transportation Commission – June 2026 (F-2, 26-1206 ) Sustainability Commission – July 2026 (F-3, 26-1502 ) Greenbelt Advisory Commission – August 6, 2026 (F-4, 26-1539 ) Employees’ Retirement System Board – August 20, 2026 (F-5, 26-1612 ) Retiree Health Care Benefit Plan & Trust Board – August 20, 2026 (F-6, 26-1613 ) Accessibility and getting the packet Everyone is encouraged to take part in public meetings.
If you need translation, sign language, or other accommodations, you can contact the City Clerk’s Office :
Phone: 734-794-6140 Email: cityclerk@a2gov.org Mail or in person: 301 E. Huron St., Ann Arbor, MI 48104 Requests made with less than two business days’ notice might not be able to be met. A paper copy of the Council packet can be made available during regular business hours if you ask the Clerk’s Office.
